text.en:
At a stadium announcement Vikram heard that 1,00,000 people had bought tickets. His uncle said, "In India we say one lakh. In other countries they say one hundred thousand."
"Same number, different names!" laughed Vikram.

In the Indian system the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, lakhs, ten lakhs, crores and so on. Commas are placed after the first three digits from the right and then after every two digits: 12,34,56,789.
In the international system the commas come after every three digits: 123,456,789. One lakh is 100,000 (one hundred thousand). Ten lakh is one million (1,000,000). One crore is ten million (10,000,000).
To compare large numbers, compare the number of digits first; the number with more digits is bigger. If the digits are the same, compare from the leftmost digit.
In the Indian system we write commas after the first three digits and then after every two digits.
One lakh is one hundred thousand. Ten lakh is one million.
To compare big numbers, count the digits first, then compare from the left.

problem.en: Write 12345678 using commas in the Indian system.

text.en: Start from the right. Put a comma after the first three digits: 678.
Then put commas after every two digits: 45, then 23, then 1.

why.en: One crore, twenty three lakh, forty five thousand, six hundred seventy eight.

prompt.en: A friend says 10 lakh and 1 million are different numbers. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Ten lakh is 10,00,000 and one million is 1,000,000. They are the same number.
The names differ between the two systems.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking different names mean different values.

points.en: Indian system: commas after 3 digits, then every 2 digits.
More digits means a bigger number.
